text: Variables are containers that store data, and assignment uses the equals sign — the name on the left, the value on the right.
Here we create four variables at once: age holds a whole number, an integer.
Name holds text, which Python calls a string, always wrapped in quotes.
Score holds a decimal number, a float, and is_student holds True or False, a boolean.
Notice you never declare the type — Python looks at the value and figures out the type automatically.
You can check it yourself with the built-in type function, which reports exactly what kind of value you're holding.
[chuckle] Python also lets you assign several variables on a single line — x, y, and z all at once, matched up by position.
And because Python is dynamically typed, a variable isn't locked to one type forever.
[clear throat] Watch — we reassign age from the number twenty-five to the text twenty-five, and Python accepts it without a single error.
Up next, numbers and math. Follow so you don't miss it.
